atlas_home_region_card.compact: Acoustic song as public argument, community memory, and movement language.

region_scene_page.compact: The folk revival drew from older ballads, labor songs, blues, gospel, and topical writing, then placed them in coffeehouses, festivals, campuses, and civil-rights contexts.
region_scene_page.standard: The folk revival drew from older ballads, labor songs, blues, gospel, and topical writing, then placed them in coffeehouses, festivals, campuses, and civil-rights contexts. Bob Dylan's Don't Think Twice, It's All Right, Joan Baez, Pete Seeger, and Woody Guthrie give the scene its high-recognition landmarks.
region_scene_page.deep: The folk revival drew from older ballads, labor songs, blues, gospel, and topical writing, then placed them in coffeehouses, festivals, campuses, and civil-rights contexts. The performance often sounds deliberately plain so the words and group participation stay central. Bob Dylan's Don't Think Twice, It's All Right, Joan Baez, Pete Seeger, and Woody Guthrie give the scene its high-recognition landmarks. From there, the examples move from quick recognition toward medium and deeper scene signals.
